facts.text: The CloudWatch log group for a Lambda function is created automatically.
The Lambda execution role has the logs:CreateLogGroup permission.
The Lambda execution role has the logs:PutLogEvents permission.
The Lambda function completes at least one successful invocation.
A Lambda function can appear to run successfully while no logs are written.
No error is surfaced when no logs are written.
Nothing indicates that logging has failed when no logs are written.
A Lambda function seems healthy but produces no logs.
The execution role should be checked for both logs:CreateLogGroup and logs:PutLogEvents.
The function should be confirmed to have completed at least one successful invocation.
The log group is not created automatically.
A missing permission shows up as a function that appears to run successfully with no logs written.

repair.regen_doc:
The CloudWatch log group for a Lambda function is created automatically, but only when all of the following conditions hold: the Lambda execution role has the logs:CreateLogGroup permission, the execution role has the logs:PutLogEvents permission, and the function completes at least one successful invocation. If any one of these is missing, the log group is not created automatically.

This matters because of how a missing permission shows up in practice. A function can appear to run successfully while no logs are written. When no logs are written, no error is surfaced, so nothing indicates that logging has failed. If a function seems healthy but produces no logs, check that the execution role has both logs:CreateLogGroup and logs:PutLogEvents, and confirm that the function has completed at least one successful invocation.
